title: An account somebody else is using
for: Sign-ins or actions by an account that its owner did not make.

steps.title: Revoke the account's sessions and tokens in the identity provider
steps.why: A password change leaves every session already open still open.

steps.title: Reset the password and re-enrol the second factor
steps.why: The attacker may have added a factor of their own; resetting only the password keeps theirs.

steps.title: Suspend the account if it cannot be secured at once
steps.why: A suspended account does no more harm while the rest is worked out.
steps.undo: Unsuspend the account in the identity provider once its sessions and factors are clean.

steps.title: List the account's second factors, recovery addresses and app passwords and remove any its owner does not recognise
steps.why: These are how access survives a reset.

steps.title: List OAuth grants, API tokens and mail forwarding rules and remove any its owner does not recognise
steps.why: A forwarding rule or a granted app keeps reading after the account is recovered.

steps.title: Read what the account did while it was not its owner's: sign-ins, data read, changes made
steps.why: What was reached decides whether personal data was involved, and so which clocks start.

steps.title: Decide, on the incident, whether a breach has likely occurred
steps.why: The deadlines run from that decision, not from the end of this list.

steps.title: Tell the account's owner what happened and what they need to do
steps.why: They will otherwise find out from a sign-in prompt, and approve the next one.
